To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transcriptome divergence in normal and cancer cell lines is described by statistical geometry and the geometry is different in the two cases.

transcriptomes of cell types exhibit a tree structure that can be detected using a statistical model, that the tree structure is more pronounced in normal cells than in cancer cells, and that the tree structure of normal cell transcriptomes is consistent with the sister cell-type evolutionary model of cell-type origination.

1) cell types have a tree-like gene expression structure that reflects their evolutionary relationships; 2) cancer cell lines have a less structured gene expression structure; 3) this difference in structure can be used to predict the cell-type origin of cancer samples; and 4) the statistical model we develop can be used to detect tree structures in other types of data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical geometry of transcriptomic data.
the statistical geometry of transcriptomes, and how it is affected by the evolution of cell types and the emergence of cancer.
the statistical geometry of transcriptomic data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sister cell-type hypothesis is a valid model of cell-type evolution.
the tree-like organization is a feature of normal cell types and is lost in cancer cells.
the tree structure is present in transcriptomic data of normal cells but absent in the transcriptomic data of cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell type evolution is a process that can be described as the evolution of gene expression programs, which can be quantified using transcriptomics.
the evolution of cell types is a tree-like process, but cancer is not.
the transcriptome of normal cells is structured in a tree-like manner, and this tree structure can be detected by our statistical model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell-type evolution is not a random process but rather one that is highly structured and predictable.
the statistical structure of transcriptomes is a promising avenue for studying the evolution of cell types.
transcriptomic data from normal and diseased tissue are amenable to a statistical framework for studying the geometry of gene expression.
